item.title: Living with water: Listening to rivers and wetlands is no longer optional in Goa
item.description: Goa faces a water crisis despite abundant rainfall, driven by poor planning and unchecked development. Pollution and erosion threaten rivers and wetlands, impacting livelihoods. Community-led projects like Goa Water Stories highlight the need for sustainable water management to preserve balance.

item.title: Scientists map rare earthquakes deep within Earth’s mantle for the first time
item.description: Stanford researchers have mapped rare mantle earthquakes globally, revealing clusters beneath the Himalayas and Bering Strait. This breakthrough distinguishes mantle quakes from crustal ones, enhancing our understanding of deep earthquake origins and Earth's internal mechanics.

item.title: January 2026 fifth warmest on record despite cold snap in Europe, North America
item.description: January 2026 was the fifth warmest on record, with Europe and North America facing cold snaps due to a wavy Arctic jet stream, while the Southern Hemisphere experienced extreme heat and wildfires. Sea surface temperatures remained high, and sea ice extent was notably low.

item.title: Replacing humans with machines is leaving truckloads of food stranded and unusable
item.description: Automation in food supply chains is causing disruptions, leaving food stranded due to digital system failures. The reliance on AI and data-driven systems over human intervention is creating vulnerabilities, as seen in recent cyberattacks. Human oversight and transparent algorithms is crucial.

item.title: Sixth year of drought in Texas and Oklahoma leaves ranchers bracing for another harsh summer
item.description: The Southern Plains, especially Texas and Oklahoma, face a sixth year of severe drought, forcing ranchers to sell cattle and causing billions in agricultural losses. Climate patterns and rising temperatures exacerbate the situation, with no immediate relief in sight.
